appraisal_events.evidence: "la gentille admiration de Robert... se complétait d'une si entière assimilation de leurs idées, qu'au bout de quarante-huit heures il avait oublié que ces idées n'étaient pas de lui"; Saint-Loup then "crut devoir me souhaiter la bienvenue avec chaleur et m'approuver" as though the narrator's own thesis were poaching on Saint-Loup's territory ("chasser sur ses terres").
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes a comic flaw in Robert: his admiration is so total that he unconsciously absorbs the narrator's own idea as his own, then patronizingly 'welcomes' the narrator to an idea the narrator had originated, revealing a gap between Robert's assumed intellectual authorship and the reality.

status_effects.explanation: Robert is locally shown to be unwittingly vain and forgetful of the true origin of his own opinions, softly undercutting the earlier picture of him as sharp and discerning.

The narrator's own thesis proves persuasive enough that Robert absorbs it wholesale as his own thinking, quietly affirming the narrator's intellectual influence even as Robert believes himself the host of the idea.

ambiguities: The narrator's diagnosis of Robert's idea-absorption is framed affectionately ('la gentille admiration'), which tempers what might otherwise read as sharper mockery; the diminishment is real but muted by evident warmth, so its magnitude is kept modest.
